data.description:
## Report (from a rebar client)
A Rebar CLI quirk treated `create task --help` as a literal task and created an accidental placeholder ticket.

## Observed
Running `rebar create task --help` (an attempt to view help for the create-task command) does NOT print help — instead the parser consumes `--help` as the positional title argument, so a ticket titled `--help` (a placeholder) is actually CREATED.

## Expected
`create task --help` (and `--help`/`-h` on any create subcommand) should print the command's usage/help and create NOTHING. Help must never be interpreted as ticket content.

## Impact
Accidental placeholder tickets pollute the store and require cleanup; the write side-effect on a help request is surprising and violates least-astonishment.

## Notes / possible cause
The create command path likely reads the first positional as the title before any --help interception. Compare with the argparse standardization landed for the write commands (claim/transition, ticket fd48-7a80-33e9-4400): --help there is served byte-exact by the top-level dispatcher and never reaches the handler. The create path may bypass that dispatcher help interception, or accept a bare positional that swallows `--help`. Needs repro + root-cause.

## Repro
1. `rebar create task --help`
2. Observe: no help text; a new ticket titled `--help` is created (verify via `rebar list`).
data.title: create task --help treated as a literal task title, creating an accidental placeholder ticket
